description: rational resampler 5/3 on complex samples vs rational_resampler_ccf

fixed_vs_float.rationale: Taps rounded to Q15 (sum of |tap rounding error| 3.501164105090706e-4) acting on an input peak of 0.705 FS per component, plus 0.5 LSB of output rounding (Q15) and 0.02 Q15 LSB for the f32 reference itself; per component <= 8.608193250390663 Q15 LSB, x sqrt(2) for the complex magnitude. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

Taps rounded to Q15 (sum of |tap rounding error| 3.501164105090706e-4) acting on an input peak of 0.705 FS per component, plus 1.0 LSB of output rounding (Q15) and 0.02 Q15 LSB for the f32 reference itself; per component <= 9.108193250390663 Q15 LSB, x sqrt(2) for the complex magnitude. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

Taps rounded to Q17 (sum of |tap rounding error| 7.193280148056982e-5) acting on an input peak of 0.705 FS per component, plus 0.5 LSB of output rounding (Q17) and 0.02 Q15 LSB for the f32 reference itself; per component <= 1.8067512974352948 Q15 LSB, x sqrt(2) for the complex magnitude. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

float_vs_gnuradio.rationale: f32 rounding in an 41-tap sum: each of the n additions errs by at most 2^-24 of the partial sum (<= peak * sum|taps| = 4.981374954058003); twice that covers both evaluation orders (GNU Radio uses SIMD kernels): 1.1283 Q15 LSB. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

name: rational_resampler_ccf_5_3
reference_shift_note: GNU Radio's first output is the full-rate filter output at position (K-1)*I = 40 (K = taps per branch); ours counts from 0 with :phase = 1, so GNU Radio output m is our output m + 13.
